registers: MECHANISM ATTRIBUTION for the one cell PR #93 left above the HBM3 parity band: down/T=32 read D_graphed/G_graphed = 1.695 against [0.9, 1.4] while the other three cells sat inside it. This registration names three candidate mechanisms, the observables that separate them, and graded bands for the shape claims — stamped before any card is rented and before the scan code has produced a single timed number on any device.

the_anomaly_and_the_clue_already_in_hand.source: graphed_buckets_hbm3/graphed_buckets_race.json (merged, PR #93) and graphed_buckets/graphed_buckets_race.json (merged, PR #90) — existing data, used only to FORM the hypotheses; every graded number below comes from a new run.
the_anomaly_and_the_clue_already_in_hand.the_flip: On GDDR6 the D-arm's excess over G is ~byte-proportional (gate_up, with 2x down's bytes and FLOPs, pays ~1.6x down's excess). On HBM3 the ORDER FLIPS: down pays 1.6x GATE_UP's excess despite half the work. Byte-proportional traffic cannot produce the flip, so on H100 the excess in that cell is not (mainly) memory traffic.

candidate_mechanisms.H_floor: Per-kernel execution floor times kernel count. The D graph at lora=False is a per-expert python loop captured whole: dequant + F.linear forward and a dgrad GEMM backward per expert, ~3E GEMM/dequant kernels plus elementwise — order 200+ kernels against the fused arm's handful. At R small enough that each kernel's work is below its floor, D pays ~count x floor regardless of bytes. Arithmetic sanity: ~190 extra kernels x ~3 us ~= 0.6 ms, the observed down excess. Weakness: a pure floor story predicts roughly EQUAL excess for both projections (same kernel count), not down > gate_up.
candidate_mechanisms.H_select: Shape-dependent cuBLAS kernel selection. down's per-expert GEMMs ([R,1024]x[1024,2048] fwd, [R,2048]x[2048,1024] dgrad) may select a different kernel family on sm_90 than gate_up's ([R,2048]x[2048,2048]) — e.g. a splitK variant with an extra reduction kernel and workspace traffic. This program has already caught shape-dependent selection twice (Ada F.linear large-M, leg 1; bmm batch-shape, graphed-buckets amendment 1). Predicts the excess LOCALIZES in named GEMM-family kernels and can differ by projection at equal kernel-loop structure.
candidate_mechanisms.H_traffic: Memory bytes bind. Already the confirmed story on GDDR6 (PR #90) and REFUTED for the H100 down cell by the flip above; retained as the null against which the scan's R-dependence is read.

design_uniform_full_R_scan.cells: proj in {gate_up, down} x R in {1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128}, OLMoE-1B-7B census shapes, E=64, lora=FALSE (matching the anomalous race cells exactly), fwd+bwd, both arms as DenseGroupsStep('fused'|'base') captured and replayed — the merged PR #90 machinery, unmodified.
design_uniform_full_R_scan.uniform_full: Every expert gets EXACTLY R real rows (sizes=[R]*E, zero padding, waste ratio 1.0). The D arm's per-expert kernel SHAPES are R-determined and identical to the race's padded slices, so the anomaly's kernels are reproduced exactly while the padding confound is removed; T_real = E*R varies with R by construction and these cells are NOT comparable to race cells and license no throughput claim.
design_uniform_full_R_scan.instrument: REPLAY-ONLY timed blocks (load() once, outside the timed region, then n replays), interleaved g_a, g_b, d_a, d_b with per-arm self-pairs; cell VOID if either self-pair falls outside [0.967, 1.033]. This DELIBERATELY diverges from race_cell's load-inclusive loop: load() is an arm-shared additive host cost that dilutes every ratio hardest at small R, which would fail P1 for an instrument reason rather than a mechanism reason — the exact band-vs-comparator mismatch that killed F4 twice. The load-inclusive quantity is still measured and REPORTED per cell (one block per arm) so the scan stays comparable to the race's numbers; it grades nothing.
design_uniform_full_R_scan.hardware: One SECURE H100 SXM pod, SHARED HOST ALLOWED — deliberate second application of PR #93's refined rule (graphed bands wider than ~±3% are valid on shared pods; every graded band here is ordinal or >=10%). Teardown per standing discipline, hard $35 cap (expected ~$1).
design_uniform_full_R_scan.profile_pass: torch.profiler (CUDA activity) over 3 replays per arm at R in {8, 32}, both projections: kernel count per replay, per-kernel-family self time (gemm/dequant/fused-triton/elementwise by name), top-12 kernels by device self time with VERBATIM names. POSITIVE CONTROL: profiling 3 eager fused steps must return >0 kernel records, else the profiler is blind on this pod and every profile field is VOID — attribution then reads 'unattributed (instrument blind)', not a mechanism verdict.
design_uniform_full_R_scan.floor_probe: A captured chain of 256 data-dependent scalar adds, replay-timed: per-kernel replay floor on this pod, REPORTED as a yardstick, never subtracted from anything.

graded_bands.P1_ratio_declines_with_R: Spearman rank correlation of (D/G wall ratio) against R over the 8 scan points, per projection: rho <= -0.7 for BOTH projections. Falsifier: a flat or rising profile in either projection kills the floor-dilution reading of the race's own four points (1.695/1.245 at R=32 vs 1.178/1.147 at R=128) and the anomaly needs a mechanism that does not dilute with per-kernel work.
graded_bands.P2_the_flip_replicates: At R=32: excess ratio [mean(d_a,d_b)-mean(g_a,g_b)]_down / [same]_gate_up >= 1.1. Falsifier: the flip was an artifact of the race's routing draws or a one-off, and H_select loses its footing (the anomaly then needs re-observation before more mechanism work).
graded_bands.P4_floor_regime_exists: D-arm time elasticity from R=1 to R=8, e = log(t(8)/t(1))/log(8), <= 0.35 for BOTH projections (8x the work costing at most ~2.07x the time). Falsifier: D-arm time scales near-linearly from R=1, there is no floor regime at these sizes on H100, and H_floor is dead as stated.

P3_attribution_decision_rules_NOT_a_grad: Which mechanism carries the down excess is answered from the profile, verbatim, by pre-named rules — registered as rules rather than a numeric band because no prior profile of these graphs on this card exists and this program's newest law forbids grading a band calibrated on anything other than the arm it grades (PR #93, F4, falsified twice). Rules: (a) if D-down's GEMM-family kernel count per replay exceeds D-gate_up's, or splitK/reduction kernel names appear in down's table and not gate_up's -> H_select. (b) if counts are equal and down's per-GEMM-kernel mean duration >= gate_up's despite half the FLOPs, with both near the floor probe's yardstick -> H_floor with a per-kernel floor that is shape-insensitive below R*. (c) if the excess sits outside GEMM-family kernels entirely (dequant or elementwise) -> neither named mechanism; report as unattributed-with-location. (d) profiler positive control fails -> unattributed (instrument blind).
stop_rule: Verbatim write-up of P1/P2/P4 and the P3 rule outcomes, including falsifications and voids. No band adjustment after data. Spearman needs >= 6 live points per projection, P2 needs both R=32 cells live, P4 needs R in {1,8} live for both projections — any shortfall is a REFUSAL for that gate, written as such. No re-runs for a better number; instrument voids follow the self-pair rule only.
what_a_pass_licenses: A mechanism NAME for the above-band cell in RESULTS-graphed-buckets.md and, if H_select, a concrete follow-up target (the offending kernel selection, filed against the projection shape). It licenses NO throughput claim of any kind: uniform-full cells measure kernel scaling, not a workload.
